Why New York generates MT demand

The New York market runs on infrastructure — power generation across the state, the harbour and its terminals, one of the world's largest transit systems, and the structural steel that a continuously rebuilding city consumes.

Turbine components, boiler headers and structural welds take MT during outages — surface cracking at stub welds and attachment details is a known header mechanism.

In-process MT on fit-ups, tack repairs and completed structural welds catches surface defects while rework is cheap.

Class surveys call MT on hatch corners, crane pedestals, rudder horns and other fatigue-prone details, where the finding decides steel renewal scope.

Wheelsets, axles and bogie frames pass through MT during overhaul, where fatigue cracking is the dominant find.

What typically gets examined

In practice that means MT work across generating station pressure parts, bridge and building structural steel, port and terminal equipment, and subway and commuter rail infrastructure — with scope set by the damage mechanisms each asset actually runs, not by a standard menu.

Certification and acceptance in New York

New York State boiler law and NBIC govern statutory equipment; structural work on public projects carries AWS D1.1 CWI inspection requirements written into contract, and transit work follows the authorities' own engineering standards with night-possession scheduling.

Examinations themselves are performed to ASME Section V Article 7, ASTM E709 and E1444, and the ISO 9934 series, with acceptance from the governing construction code. The evidence chain — technician certification current on the day, instrument and reference block calibration, and the procedure revision in force — travels with every report, because that bundle is what an audit actually checks.
